extracted.intended_audience: BBC audiences, platform partners (search/social) and journalists interested in BBC editorial standards
extracted.subtask_description: Official BBC News guidance describing the editorial standards, transparency indicators and machine-readable labels used to help audiences and platforms judge the trustworthiness of BBC online journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial values: accuracy, impartiality, independence and honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC strives for journalism that is accurate, impartial, independent and fair; committed to achieving the highest standards of accuracy and impartiality and to avoid knowingly or materially misleading audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted editorial values: 'The trust that our audience has in all our content underpins everything that we do. We are independent, impartial and honest. We are committed to achieving the highest standards of accuracy and impartiality and strive to avoid knowingly or materially misleading our audiences.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: In all our output we will treat every subject with an impartiality that reflects the full range of views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance adds: 'We will consider all the relevant facts fairly and with an open mind.' Implicit anti-pattern: presenting a narrow set of views or failing to reflect the full range of relevant opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: act in the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of the BBC is to act in the public interest, serving all audiences through the provision of impartial, high-quality and distinctive output and services that inform, educate and entertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames editorial decision-making and underpins expectations of public‑interest reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and disclosure of ownership/funding
rubrics_metrics.description: We are independent of outside interests and arrangements that could undermine our editorial integrity; audiences should be confident decisions are not influenced by outside interests, political or commercial pressures, or personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes links to BBC Charter on independence, Framework Agreement and guidance on commercial activities to show how ownership/funding safeguards are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics policy / adherence to Editorial Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC's Editorial Guidelines outline the editorial values and practices that all output is expected to conform to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page links to specific Editorial Guidelines sections (Impartiality, Editorial Standards, Conflicts of Interest, Accuracy, Accountability, Removal of Online Content, etc.) as the detailed rules that implement the high‑level values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment to diversity in coverage and staffing, and transparency about progress (e.g., Diversity Staffing Report, Equality Information Report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References Editorial Guidelines section on Impartiality and Diversity of Opinion and provides links to Diversity and Inclusion pages and staffing reports as evidence of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Committed to achieving due accuracy and being open in acknowledging mistakes; policies on corrections are set out in Editorial Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an article is edited to correct a material inaccuracy a note with the date will be added at the end; small errors that do not alter editorial meaning may be corrected without a note. Presumption that online material is permanently accessible unless exceptional circumstances (legal reasons, personal safety risks, serious editorial breach) require removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and fact‑checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Output should be well sourced, based on sound evidence, thoroughly tested and presented in clear, precise language; be honest about what we don't know and avoid unfounded speculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Guidelines on Accuracy set out the specifics; claims, allegations and material facts that cannot be corroborated should normally be attributed. Links also to Ofcom Operating Framework and Licence for the BBC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on unnamed/anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC has a policy and guidance on the use of anonymous sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references the Editorial Guidelines for detailed rules (e.g., mandatory referrals, gathering material, user contributions) rather than listing the full rules inline—implicit expectation: anonymous sourcing is governed and restricted by Editorial Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable feedback and complaints procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear processes for audience feedback and complaints are provided (BBC Complaints Framework; Have Your Say; Contact Us).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BBC encourages audience engagement and provides routes for corrections, complaints and questions as part of accountability and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist expertise and bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles based on original reporting carry bylines; many correspondents and editors' bylines link to biographical pages showing expertise and social media details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General news stories that compile multiple sources or are produced by several members of staff do not as a rule carry bylines. Providing bylines and author bios is used as an indicator of journalist expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine‑readable type-of-work labels
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC News uses machine‑readable labels in six categories to indicate the type of content: News, Analysis, Ask the Audience, Explainer, Opinion, Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to make clear what kind of information the reader is consuming and to allow search engines and social platforms to identify reliable journalism via structured metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type label — News
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism based on facts, either observed and verified directly by the reporter, or reported and verified from knowledgeable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to denote straightforward factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type label — Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Output primarily based on the specialist knowledge of an author, whether a BBC journalist or outside expert, to help you understand complex current affairs and trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals interpretative/contextual material rather than straight reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type label — Ask the Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Content created primarily to elicit direct audience response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates participatory content intended to gather audience input rather than strictly report facts or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type label — Explainer
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that provides clear factual explanation of the causes or context behind the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to signal explanatory journalism focused on clarity and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type label — Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Expressions of personal views by outside experts, advocating ideas and drawing conclusions based on the author's interpretation of facts and data; BBC News itself is impartial and does not offer opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels distinguish opinion pieces from impartial BBC journalism to avoid conflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type label — Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Content based on a critical appraisal of an event, a work of art etc, containing first‑hand opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals evaluative, subjective content (e.g., arts reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and references / sourcing transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Output should, as appropriate, be well‑sourced and link to official reports, statistics and other sources to enable readers to judge underlying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on a single source for a key aspect, the BBC will strive to credit that source; whenever appropriate the BBC offers links to relevant third‑party websites that provide additional information, source material or informed comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology disclosure for in‑depth work
rubrics_metrics.description: For complex investigations or data journalism, BBC will show the underlying data and disclose any caveats, assumptions or methodological frameworks used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of methodological details to disclose include study design, sample size, representativeness, margins of error, how the data was collected, geographical relevance and time periods. Purpose: help readers understand how the work was done and assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine‑readability of trust indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators of trustworthy journalism are being made machine‑readable so they can be picked up by search engines and social media platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps platforms identify reliable sources and surfaces contextual metadata (e.g., type labels, bylines, methodology links).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of permanence and conditions for removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless content is specifically made available only for a limited time, there is a presumption that material published online will become part of a permanently accessible archive and will not normally be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptional circumstances permitting removal include legal reasons, personal safety risks, or a serious breach of editorial standards that cannot be rectified except by removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisational provenance and transparency (founding date, leadership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context about the organisation (e.g., founding date, leadership such as BBC News Board) to help audiences understand provenance and governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page includes links to history of the BBC and to meet the senior executive team—used as background transparency that supports trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial activities and conflicts of interest management
rubrics_metrics.description: Frameworks and agreements exist to manage commercial activities and prevent conflicts that could affect editorial integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links provided to BBC Framework Agreement on provision of commercial activities and Guidelines for BBC Commercial Services; these documents explain how commercial activity is governed to protect editorial independence.
